newsitem.title: USA: CBO seen giving U.S. economic assumptions early.
newsitem.headline: CBO seen giving U.S. economic assumptions early.

text.p: The Office of Management and Budget expects the Congressional Budget Office to provide it with the economic assumptions underlying CBO's budget forecast early, possibly next week, an OMB spokesman said on Monday.
"We understand that they plan to give us the economic assumptions," said OMB spokesman Larry Haas, adding that this may occur early next week.

In doing so, the CBO, at the direction of Congressional Republicans, would be giving OMB the figures in time to help prepare for its February budget submission. Normally, CBO's figures would not be available until next year.

However, the spokesman said that CBO was not expected to provide all of its data, leaving out "technical assumptions" on the government's expected revenues and the expected rate of spending on the Medicare and Medicaid programs.

Separately, the spokesman confirmed a New York Times story published on Monday suggesting that the difference between the 2002 budget deficit estimates by the CBO and OMB has narrowed to around $50 billion.
"We expect them to be somewhere in the area of $150 billion," Haas said, adding that OMB's own figures were expected to be closer to $100 billion.
The narrowing in the figures should make it easier to balance the federal budget.
